rationale.conceptual: The constitutive model is a paper-specific, multi-axial, history-dependent formulation with a switching surface, back-stress/back-field potentials, saturation enforcement, and a backward Euler integrator. The steady-state FE procedure adds the complexity of translating crack-tip field equations into a custom iterative solver. These are interacting, non-trivial components that demand real understanding beyond off-the-shelf libraries.
rationale.execution: Building a full finite element model (mesh, assembly, iterative steady-state solver with streamline integration of the constitutive law) and implementing the I-integral contour evaluation constitute a multi-stage engineering pipeline. Running it for 14 distinct electrical loading conditions, each requiring a binary search to match G_tip = G_0, adds operational complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The core work is implementing a custom constitutive model for ferroelectric domain switching and a steady-state crack growth FE solver. The method is non-trivial, requiring deep understanding of nonlinear mechanics, FE programming, and iterative solution of coupled electromechanical fields. The pipeline is substantial (FE from scratch, streamline integration, binary search for toughness ratio).
